items.title: Anthropic study: analysts went with their AI agent's randomly assigned lean 86% of the time
items.summary: In a randomized trial, 50 professional causal-inference analysts worked a fictional farm-policy analysis with Claude Code. A coin flip set which of two defensible options each analyst's agent leaned toward on four analytical decisions. Analysts matched the lean 86% of the time against 50% by chance (92%, 82%, 81%, 90% per decision), and switched away from their own stated preference 60% of the time when the agent disagreed versus 6% when it agreed. Afterward 77% reused the agent's arguments but only 15% credited it. The authors note the lean was deliberately strengthened for the study.

reception.summary: Replies focus on the 77% versus 15% attribution gap and suggest writing down your own call before the agent weighs in, or asking the agent for the strongest counter-argument. No one disputed the design; one reply asked whether pre-commitment would change the 60% switch rate.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra beats Astra on Roboflow vision benchmarks at about 92% lower cost
items.summary: Roboflow's Piotr Skalski reports GPT-6.1 Terra outscoring GPT-6.1 Astra on all three of their vision benchmark tracks (text, object detection, counting) while running about 47% faster and costing about 92% less. He says he re-ran the results to double-check.

doubt.pushback: A reply points out one example scores 46 of 46 objects counted but only 60.8 mAP@50, so counts can look right while boxes or classes are wrong; another asks whether the scores were tracked over time.

reception.summary: Builders say the price gap changes what they would ship, and one plans to swap Gemini Argon for Terra on a large classification job. Skeptical replies question count-versus-box accuracy and possible drift; one dismisses the result as a newer small model winning select tasks.

items.title: ParseBench adds GPT-6.1 Terra: 5th overall, strong on tables, weak on layout and charts
items.summary: LlamaIndex ran GPT-6.1 Terra through its ParseBench document-parsing benchmark. It ranks 5th overall at about 1 cent per page, scores well on tables and poorly on layout and chart extraction.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-run benchmark from a company that sells a competing parser.

items.title: Letta FrontierMemory leaderboard: Kimi K3.1 Pro ties for first, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash beats pricier models
items.summary: Letta added GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to its FrontierMemory agent-memory leaderboard. Kimi K3.1 Pro ties Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 for first, and V4.1 Flash scores above GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon at a fraction of their cost.

items.title: Cartesia Managed Agents scores 1115 Elo on Artificial Analysis Speech Agent Arena, up 98 over Cartesia Line
items.summary: Artificial Analysis rates Cartesia's new Managed Agents at Elo 1115 (95% CI 1086 to 1144, 685 samples) in its Speech Agent Arena, 98 points above Cartesia Line at 1017. Task success rose from 77.5% to 91.7%. The configuration tested used GPT-5.5 as the reasoning model.

items.title: Hermes Agent adds an ElevenLabs sound-effects plugin
items.summary: Nous Research shipped an ElevenLabs sound-effects plugin for Hermes Agent so the agent can generate SFX on request. Install with: hermes plugins install elevenlabs-sound-effects.

items.title: TensorFold runs on Apple M1 GPUs under Linux via a Vulkan backend, 41% faster per token
items.summary: A contributor got TensorFold inference running on an M1 Max GPU under Linux through a Vulkan backend, cutting per-token latency from 160 ms to 94 ms with byte-identical output. The work is an in-progress PR, not yet merged.

doubt.pushback: Single contributor result in an unmerged PR.

items.title: Notion AI Meeting Notes labels each speaker in Google Meet via the Chrome extension
items.summary: Notion's AI Meeting Notes Chrome extension now attributes transcript lines to individual speakers in Google Meet calls.

reception.summary: Users welcome attribution but ask about Zoom support, overlapping speakers and cloud transcription after leaving a call; one reports the extension not showing the feature on the latest version.

items.title: NVIDIA posts Metatron-v1, an ONNX humanoid walking and recovery policy for the Unitree G1
items.summary: NVIDIA quietly published nvidia/Metatron-v1 on Hugging Face under the NVIDIA Open Model License: a learned walking and fall-recovery controller for the Unitree G1, exported as a single-robot demo ONNX and a six-robot batched ONNX. It is a robotics policy, not a language model. The card reports only export parity checks; there is no training checkpoint, dataset, paper or task-success benchmark.

doubt.pushback: No announcement or benchmarks; the card says its numbers are export checks, not task-success or real-robot results.

items.title: TaskNet: AI interviews build occupational task lists that cover more real work than O*NET
items.summary: Stanford, Mercor, the O*NET Center and NBER researchers used an AI interviewer with 132 workers across six occupations to produce 202 validated task statements, including 79 with no O*NET counterpart. TaskNet covers 89% of tasks reported by held-out workers versus 79% for O*NET, and it shifts AI exposure estimates, raising them for software developers and lawyers.

security_forwarded.matched: always_forward: software supply chain (npm, GitHub Actions); agent tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI hooks); stack: Node.js, Bun, Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Antigravity
security_forwarded.note: JFrog (2026-10-26, also Corgea, The Register) found the testmetest / @iobandamwer npm worm armed 42 real GitHub repos across 11 hijacked owners with a 12.9 to 13.7 MB .github/init.js plus startup hooks: .claude/settings.json SessionStart runs 'node .github/init.js || bun .github/init.js', and .gemini/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .vscode/tasks.json do the same, so opening or starting an agent session in a cloned repo runs it. GitHub code search and the contents API miss the oversized blobs. The payload steals GitHub/npm/cloud/SSH and Claude/Codex/Gemini/Copilot tokens, abuses npm OIDC trusted publishing, installs pkg-runtime (~/.local/share/runtimes/sync.py) and net-health-checker (~/.local/bin/net-health-checker.sh), and the latter runs rm -rf ~/ if the stolen GitHub token starts returning 401/403. Fix: remove the persistence services BEFORE revoking tokens, then rotate all credentials; audit repos via the Git trees API for those hook files; delete chore/ci-* and deps/upd-* branches; block 43.228.157.68 and aiarmor.website; be wary of packages running native .node addons from postinstall (.napi_cache). Box check: no testmetest packages, no init.js hooks, no net-health-checker or sync.py persistence.

security_forwarded.matched: always_forward: agent tooling (MCP servers); stack: Python
security_forwarded.note: CVE-2026-116684 (GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23, CVSS 6.8 Medium, CWE-863): the MCP Python SDK (pip 'mcp') 1.10.0 to 1.29.1 and 2.0.0 to 2.1.1 server-side bearer auth did not check token audience, so an HTTP MCP server using AuthSettings with a token_verifier accepts tokens issued for another service by the same authorization server. Fix: upgrade to mcp 1.30.0 or 2.2.0, AND set validate_token_resource=True with resource_server_url, and return the audience as AccessToken.resource from verify_token (upgrading alone changes nothing). Workaround: reject tokens whose aud lacks your server in verify_token. Only matters for self-hosted HTTP MCP servers using SDK bearer auth. Box check: no mcp Python package installed.
